outcome: Maternal complications (postpartum hemorrhage, sepsis, Caesarean section rates)
Fetal/neonatal mortality and morbidity (acute foetal distress, asphyxia, NICU admissions)
cohort: The study included a total of 64 patients, divided into two groups for comparison of post-term pregnancies with term pregnancies.
finding: Post-term pregnancies were associated with increased risks for both mothers (postpartum hemorrhage, sepsis, higher Caesarean section rates due to acute foetal distress) and fetuses (asphyxia, NICU admissions) compared to term pregnancies.
mod_finding: Acute foetal distress was a prevalent indication for Caesarean section rates in the post-term group, and IOL is suggested as a strategy to lessen risks.
birth_weight: Fetal weight measurements were obtained and analyzed.
gest_age: The study compared pregnancies beyond 40 weeks gestation (post-term) with term pregnancies.
